title: CI has been red on main since 2026-08-27 and the tagged release commit never ran it at all
body:
## Summary

**CI has been red on `main` since 2026-08-27, through the entire 0.1.0 release, and nobody looked.** The release's `## Verified` section was assembled from local gate seals on macOS while GitHub Actions was failing on Ubuntu and on shellcheck.

**And the tagged commit has never had CI run against it at all.** `tests.yml` fires on push to `main`; `e22d9a3` and `2456ac6` were pushed together, so only the tip got a run. There is no run whose `headSha` is `e22d9a3`.

Found 2026-09-02 while verifying that the `v0.1.0` tag push had fired the release workflow. It had -- `Release` succeeded in 19s. The red was in the next row down.

## The three runs

| commit    | date       | ubuntu  | macos   | shellcheck |
| --------- | ---------- | ------- | ------- | ---------- |
| `fc794aa` | 2026-08-27 | failure | failure | failure    |
| `91ed866` | 2026-08-29 | failure | failure | failure    |
| `2456ac6` | 2026-09-01 | failure | success | failure    |

Last green: `79bfaec`, 2026-08-25. **Six days and three pushes, one of them the release.**

## What is actually failing

**Ubuntu: 8 of 824 bats tests, 0 of them failing on macOS.** Six are the gate heartbeat; two are fleet/seam.

    not ok 293  a deps/ checkout INSIDE a worktree is a dep, not a worktree
    not ok 295  two installs with identical bytes share a seam digest; different bytes do not
    not ok 382  the gate's exit status survives a heartbeat running under a terminal
    not ok 383  THE HEARTBEAT NEVER ENTERS THE CAPTURED LOG
    not ok 384  a silent gate under a terminal announces that it is alive
    not ok 385  a CHATTY gate produces no heartbeat -- the operator can already see it is alive
    not ok 387  DEVBIN_HEARTBEAT_SECS=0 disables it under a terminal
    not ok 388  a malformed interval disables the beat rather than taking the gate down

The heartbeat cluster is almost certainly pty acquisition differing between BSD and GNU `script`, but **that is a hypothesis and nothing here has measured it.**

**shellcheck: three `info`-level findings.**

    lib/cmd/clean:166      SC2015  A && B || C is not if-then-else
    lib/cmd/fullcycle:116  SC2015  A && B || C is not if-then-else
    lib/cmd/version:268    SC2119  Use version_identity "$@" ...

## Why the local instrument could not see any of it, and said nothing about that

Two independent narrowings, and each is invisible from inside its own output:

1. **PLATFORM.** Local `test all` runs on one machine. The gate seal is a true record of a macOS run, and nothing in `.out`, `.errors` or the summary line names a platform -- so `824 tests, 0 failures` reads as a fact about devbin when it is a fact about one OS.
2. **ANALYSER VERSION.** ~~Severity: `critic-shell` runs at `>= warning` and CI has no floor.~~ **THAT WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE, 2026-09-02.** Both sides run `shellcheck -x` at the same default severity. The difference is the **binary**:

    | side       | install                | version |
    | ---------- | ---------------------- | ------- |
    | local      | brew                   | 0.11.0  |
    | CI ubuntu  | `apt-get install`      | 0.9.0   |
    | CI macos   | brew                   | 0.11.0  |

    Measured, not inferred: the exact SC2015 construct from `lib/cmd/clean` run through the local binary returns rc=0 and prints nothing, and the CI log says `shellcheck is already the newest version (0.9.0-1)`. **0.9.0 flags what 0.11.0 does not.**

    **So the two CI jobs disagree with each other as well**, and the local gate agrees with the one that is not enforcing.

    I filed the severity mechanism without measuring it, having read `critic-shell`'s honest `>= warning` note and attached it to a different instrument. **Second wrong mechanism filed today on a correct conclusion** -- see `0046`. The conclusion is untouched: the local gate reported green on lines CI was failing, and nothing on either side could see the disagreement.

**`lib/cmd/version:268` is the sharpest instance.** That SC2119 is at the call site created on 2026-09-01 by the `version_identity` Highlander fix -- the same suppression-orphan episode already on the board, whose lesson was *a suppression belongs to its call site*. The lesson was learned, the local lint went green, and the new call site has been red in CI since the moment it was written.

## The class

This is the day's recurring defect in the place it costs most: **a sound instrument, aimed one unit wide, returning clean -- and the narrow reading written into a published release note as though it were the wide one.**

It is also `0048`'s shape exactly. An empty watch list and an unread CI produce the identical green, and the reader of either cannot tell which they are holding.

## Diagnosed 2026-09-02, and what each one turned out to be

**Six of the eight are ONE cause, and it is in the harness rather than the code.** Every one fails at `tests/unit/heartbeat.bats:48`, inside the `under_pty` helper:

    script -q /dev/null bash "$f" </dev/null 2>&1

That is BSD `script`. util-linux `script` takes one file operand and wants the command in `-c`, so it is handed three where it accepts one and refuses. Test 386 -- the only heartbeat test that does not use `under_pty` -- passes on Linux.

**So the heartbeat code is not broken on Linux. It is UNVERIFIED there**, which is a different claim, and the file's own header predicted the shape: *a test without a pty proves only that it stays quiet.*

**They failed rather than passing vacuously, and that is the only reason this was recoverable.** Had the helper degraded to a non-pty run, all six would have gone green while proving nothing. The fix carries a comment forbidding exactly that fallback.

**Two real portability defects in the fleet command**, both BSD-only, both on lines whose own neighbouring comments warned about the class:

- `seam_digest` called `shasum -a 256` **directly**, bypassing `sha256_files` in `lib/helpers` -- whose comment says in terms that `shasum` is the name a minimal Linux image does not have. One decision, two copies, only one portable. Now routed through a single `sha256_run`.
- `scan` converted with a bare `date -u -r "$e"`. BSD `-r` takes an epoch; GNU `-r` takes a FILE and wants `-d @<epoch>`. **This sat two lines below `mtime_epoch`, whose comment reads "BOTH ARMS, because devbin's own clock guard upstream carries a BSD-only defect found precisely because only one arm was ever exercised."** Now `utc_from_epoch`, with both arms.

**Not yet confirmed** that these two are the cause of failures 293 and 295. They are real defects on the failing platform, found on the failing path; whether they are THE cause needs a CI run to say. Local re-runs are green and prove nothing, since every defect here is invisible on macOS.

## What is not yet known

- Whether the 8 Ubuntu failures are environment-only or real defects that macOS masks. **Until that is measured, "it is just pty differences" is a guess.**
- Whether `e22d9a3` would pass. It has never been run. Its content differs from `2456ac6` only by the fleet-audit regeneration, so it would very likely fail identically -- **likely, not measured.**

## Fix directions

1. **Make the tag a CI trigger.** `tests.yml` on `push: tags: ['v*']` as well as `main`, so a released commit is tested as the released commit rather than inheriting a neighbour's verdict.
2. **Name the platform in the seal.** A gate seal that records `uname` costs one line and stops `824 tests, 0 failures` from reading wider than it measured.
3. **PIN THE SHELLCHECK VERSION.** ~~Reconcile the two thresholds.~~ There are no thresholds to reconcile -- see the correction above. The three installers pull three answers from two versions, so the fix is that every side installs the SAME analyser. **hv approved "reconcile the thresholds" on 2026-09-02 while that premise was still wrong; the approval is recorded against the corrected fix, and hv told separately.** Pinning is also what stops this recurring: an unpinned `apt-get install shellcheck` moves under the project whenever the runner image does, and the symptom is a gate going red on a commit that changed nothing.
4. **Fix the 8.** Separately, and only after somebody measures whether they are environmental.

## What hv has to rule on, separately from the fix

**Whether `RELEASES/0.1.0.md`'s `## Verified` section gets amended.** It is a published claim, it is not false on its own terms, and it is narrower than it reads. Leaving it, footnoting it, or re-measuring it are all defensible; silently rewriting a shipped release note is not one of the three.
